With the consent of parties, the matter is heard finally.

1. The instant writ petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India claims the following reliefs:-
"i) That, the impugned order contained in Annexure P/1 and letter Annexure P/2 may kindly be quashed with all consequential effects and the respondents may kindly be directed to permit the petitioner to work in terms of agreement executed in the year of 2020 upto its effect i.e. upto 2023, in the interest of justice.
ii) Cost of the petition be awarded or any other order or direction deemed fit in the circumstances of the case be issued in the favour of the petitioner."

2. Brief facts leading to filing of the instant writ petition are as under:-
2.1 The petitioner being a society registered under the Madhya Pradesh Society Registration Act, 2009 was allotted the work of supply o f NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

3. During the currency of the contract of the petitioner for supply of nutritious food to various Aganwadi Centres situated in District Morena, the respondent No.2 issued a Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) dated 14.07.2021, inviting Expressions of Interest (EOI)
from eligible Women Self-Help Groups registered with National Urban Livelihood Mission/State Urban Livelihood Mission for the last three years and operating Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts for the work of supply of nutritious food to 315 Aganwadi Centres situated in District Morena.

5. Initially, the instant writ petition was entertained by this Court, and an interim order dated 18.08.2021 was passed whereby, status quo was directed to be maintained by the parties.

By virtue of the interim order of status quo dated 18.08.2021 being in operation, the petitioner herein completed the period of contract effective till August, 2023 and the relief NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 3 WP-15529-2021 claimed by the petitioner in the instant writ petition stood worked out by virtue of the operation of the interim order dated 18.08.2021.

Nevertheless, on the request of the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, the matter was adjourned for 08.10.2025.

He further submits that during the pendency of the petition, the contract of the petitioner for supply of Mid-Day Meals to the schools situated in District Morena has been renewed by the same committee which is also responsible for considering the renewal of the petitioner's contract for the purpose of supply of Ready-to-Eat Meals/Take Home Rations/Nutritious Food to the Aganwadi Centres.

10. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the State opposes the writ petition and submits that the period of contract of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 5 WP-15529-2021 petitioner stood expired in the year 2023.
It was contended that the petitioner had continued to operate and execute the work in question beyond the contractual period solely by virtue of the interim order passed in the instant writ petition.
Accordingly, it was urged that the petition deserves to be disposed of, as the petitioner is not entitled to any further relief.
11. By way of filing an application for amendment, the petitioner is trying to get the contract continued contrary to the circular dated 5.5.2021 (Annexure P/8).

The petitioner herein has not challenged the validity of the circular dated 5.5.2021, which specifically supersedes the earlier circulars and provides that nutritious food to the Aganwadi Centres is to be provided through Women Self-Help Groups only who possess the necessary eligibility conditions.
1 2 .

The petitioner is a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1976 and not a Self-Help Group and, therefore, is ineligible to continue with the work in question under the provisions of the circular dated 5.5.2021.
Accordingly, the State counsel submitted that the relief claimed by the petitioner through amendment application deserves to be rejected and the petition deserves to the dismissed.
13. No other point has been pressed by the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

14. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the record.

The guidelines in the aforesaid letter further emphasised that since the revised guidelines laid major stress on micronutrient fortification of the THR, it required "expert technical supervision" and that it can be achieved by using accurate machines with precision in measuring the quantity in milligrams.
The Government of India communicated the judgment in the Shagun Mahila case to all States/UTs.
The judgment nowhere mentioned that private manufacturers or contractors are allowed, and the judgment was only limited to the tender conditions applicable to eligible Mahila Mandals.

However, the Central Government communication allowed the States to supply even from manufacturers:"

The extract of a letter of Additional Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development are as under:-
"A Women's' Self Help Group (SHG) (of 10- 20 women in general, 5-20 women in difficult areas) is the primary building block of NRLM's institutional design.
The S.H.G. is an informal and unregistered group.
Under N.R.L.M., one member from each identified rural poor household, preferably a woman, is to be organized into a Self Help Group (SHGs).
These groups are formed on the basis of affinity and common bonding among members.
They are not arbitrarily put together, and more important this task is not to be performed mechanically.

It requires very sensitive facilitation, initially by an external social mobilizing agency, N.G.O or government missions and later on their own federation emerges as a sensitive support agency and takes over most of the functions being performed by the initial external support organizations.
Now SHGs are formed out of the existing BPL list.
We are attempting to switch over to a participatory identification methodology which will ensure much better inclusion of the deserving poor.

The time required capacitating groups to undertake a micro- enterprise model related to Skills and Placement. Currently, only two State Missions under NRLM have experience in undertaking micro-enterprise models for ICDS - Kerala, and Odisha.
